Automate repetitive research and testing.

Build custom tools without paying for another SaaS subscription.

---
**I rated those 5 "hedge fund" AI prompts. Average: 3.5/10.**
🥇 Macro Calendar — 6/10. The only honest one. It's prep, not alpha, and doesn't pretend otherwise.
Insider + Options — 4/10. Insider buying signal is real. The "options whale" half is mostly market-maker hedging misread as conviction.
Earnings Whiplash — 3/10. Points the right concept backwards. IV sits above realized into earnings by default. That's just IV crush.
13F Tracker — 2/10. Data is 45 days stale, longs-only. Citadel's book is market-neutral, so "Citadel is buying X" means little. And "average entry price" isn't in a 13F. It doesn't exist.
Sector Rotation — 2/10. Sector rotation is the most covered topic in finance. Nothing "quiet" about it.
**The real issue:** every input is public, free, and already priced. These confuse looking things up with having an edge.
And a prompt demanding "output 5 stocks" always returns 5 stocks — whether the data existed or not.

weposttech on August 16, 2026: "Some of the technologies that sound like science fiction are already being built.

From AI models running entirely on your computer to nuclear batteries, animal communication, cultivated meat, floating cities, and digital replicas of Earth, researchers are pushing technology into areas that would have seemed impossible a few decades ago.

Here’s what makes these developments worth watching:

• AI is becoming more independent. Open-source systems are making it possible to run powerful models locally without relying on subscriptions or constant API access.
• Biology is becoming programmable. Scientists are exploring cultivated meat, animal communication, and even the recreation of traits from extinct species.
• Entire systems could be redesigned. Transportation, energy, cities, climate forecasting, and environmental monitoring may look completely different in the decades ahead.

Not every prediction will happen exactly as imagined, but the direction of technology is getting harder to ignore.
